groups.title: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals

profiles.name: Aldar Properties
profiles.why: Strong Gulf benchmark for a developer-controlled digital sales/customer journey, digital agreements, smart-building and startup-pilot narrative.
profiles.boundary: Include as a company-reported operating-model case, not proof that its metrics are causal, independently audited or transferable to Bangladesh.

profiles.name: Emaar Development
profiles.why: Shows how analytics, digital transaction interfaces and enterprise modernization can sit inside a major developer.
profiles.boundary: Do not present “Project Hawkeye” or “Vyom” as quantified ROI; public evidence records initiatives more clearly than causal outcomes.

profiles.name: JLL
profiles.why: Exemplifies service/data distribution, internal AI adoption, workflow products and venture adjacency at institutional scale.
profiles.boundary: Do not treat prompt/user counts or investment activity as productivity, customer ROI or product maturity proof.

profiles.name: Prologis
profiles.why: Owner/operator example where logistics assets, energy, automation and data services reinforce one another.
profiles.boundary: Do not infer that employee AI adoption or portfolio scale proves a specific tool’s realized value or local fit.

profiles.name: CapitaLand Investment
profiles.why: Demonstrates physical-asset, tenant/community and commerce data loops across Asia.
profiles.boundary: Treat activity and commerce figures as company-reported; do not imply the public evidence proves a causal “platform effect.”

profiles.name: Mitsui Fudosan
profiles.why: Important Japanese customer-network and neighborhood/DX benchmark, relevant to the JCX–Japan collaboration context.
profiles.boundary: Do not turn customer scale or DX programs into a verified financial-return claim; keep this as an operating-model reference.

profiles.name: Lendlease
profiles.why: Bridges design, construction, safety, digital twins, BIM/IDD, drones and operations; also connects to a quantified OpenSpace case.
profiles.boundary: Keep historical safety/portfolio claims dated and attributed; do not assume every project uses the same stack or achieves the same result.

profiles.name: Godrej Properties
profiles.why: South Asian developer comparator for AI/property analytics, virtual visits, smart-home and customer-facing operations.
profiles.boundary: Use as regional public evidence and implementation reference, not as proof of product ROI or direct Bangladesh equivalence.

profiles.name: Autodesk Construction Cloud / Forma
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Separates a product/suite from its owner and anchors design-to-delivery, BIM, CDE and preconstruction analysis.
profiles.boundary: Do not flatten Autodesk products or claim that a suite equals one system of record; customer outcomes remain vendor-reported until reviewed.

profiles.name: Procore
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Major construction workflow reference for project controls, procurement, quality and closeout; supports several outcome cases.
profiles.boundary: Do not treat the platform as universally superior or infer outcomes from vendor case studies without metric caveats.

profiles.name: PlanRadar
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Compact example of mobile/offline issue tracking, forms, plans and handover—highly legible to a delivery-trust narrative.
profiles.boundary: Its single-source profile still requires claim review; do not imply independent deployment scale or local support from the listing.

profiles.name: OpenSpace
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Makes spatial capture an evidence system for progress, disputes, payment and handover; linked to multiple quantified cases.
profiles.boundary: Preserve capture coverage, labor baseline and counterfactual limitations; images are not automatically verified site truth.

profiles.name: Buildots
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Shows bounded AI comparing site imagery with BIM/schedules and connects directly to construction progress outcomes.
profiles.boundary: Do not generalize two customer stories into universal schedule/rework improvement; require baseline and comparison context.

profiles.name: Facilio
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Connects tenant experience, work orders, IoT/BMS and energy operations, with stronger source depth than many early-stage signals.
profiles.boundary: Keep funding/adoption and customer case claims separate; no claim that all modules or integrations are production-ready for JCX.

profiles.name: BrainBox AI
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Useful smart-building example where HVAC control, energy, carbon and comfort meet measurable baselines.
profiles.boundary: Outcomes are primarily vendor/customer reports; never convert identified or reported savings into a JCX forecast.

profiles.name: TestFit
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Clear land/site-feasibility and scenario-generation example with several bounded case studies.
profiles.boundary: Treat time/cost figures as customer estimates; local parcel, zoning, flood, cost and approval data still determine transferability.

profiles.name: LandTech
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Represents land/development pipeline intelligence and the data/trust layer behind origination decisions.
profiles.boundary: Do not present UK workflow/regulatory data as portable title or feasibility truth for Bangladesh.

profiles.name: Salesforce Real Estate Cloud
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Provides a recognizable CRM/workflow anchor for lead, marketing, service and partner journeys without confusing product and company records.
profiles.boundary: The profile has limited source depth; do not infer implementation maturity, pricing or JCX integration from brand familiarity.

profiles.name: Snapdocs
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Shows transaction/closing infrastructure and connects to a bounded quantified mortgage case.
profiles.boundary: US title, e-notary, KYC and lender context is not automatically legal or operationally transferable to Bangladesh.

profiles.name: Sell-Do
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Closest mature South Asian developer-OS signal for lead routing, inventory, visits, booking and post-sales workflow.
profiles.boundary: Company scale and case claims require attribution; do not call it a JCX recommendation or assume its data model fits local ERP/payment rules.

profiles.name: One Click LCA
profiles.groupTitle: Workflow, data, physical and climate vendors
profiles.why: Keeps embodied carbon and lifecycle assessment in the core story instead of treating climate as a decorative theme.
profiles.boundary: LCA outputs depend on boundary, factors, EPD quality and local data; a software profile is not a project carbon assurance.

profiles.name: ProQ
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: Concrete local procurement/RFQ signal that makes the “phone calls and WhatsApp” problem and venture-client pilot hypothesis tangible.
profiles.boundary: Early operating history and public claims require diligence on supplier checks, delivery, quality, ERP handoff, disputes and security; not a recommendation.

profiles.name: Barikoi
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: Local mapping/address infrastructure is a direct building block for site, catchment, delivery and project discovery.
profiles.boundary: Do not equate mapping coverage with title, parcel accuracy, planning approval or customer deployment without field validation.

profiles.name: Vextrus
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: Local AI/ERP-oriented signal that invites the question of unified JCX operating workflows.
profiles.boundary: Company-reported agents/savings are not independently verified; no replacement-ERP implication should be drawn.

profiles.name: BRKZ
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: MENA procurement/credit example linking construction materials, workflow and financing rails.
profiles.boundary: Financial-release figures require current verification; do not infer creditworthiness, supplier quality or Bangladesh regulatory fit.

profiles.name: WakeCap
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: Connects site workforce/data, construction visibility, partnerships and acquisition history in a regionally relevant delivery context.
profiles.boundary: Dated announcements and acquisitions are not audited outcome evidence; avoid implying that partnership equals deployment success.

profiles.name: Landeed
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: Strong title-evidence/data-graph benchmark for a trust-critical land workflow.
profiles.boundary: State-level integrations and legal/registry conditions are not portable; never describe it as title verification in Bangladesh.

profiles.name: Truzo
profiles.groupTitle: Bangladesh, South Asia and MENA signals
profiles.why: Explicitly pilot-stage local signal for construction dispute/expense evidence, useful for showing how local experimentation should be framed.
profiles.boundary: “Now in pilot” and “zero disputes” remain company claims; show as pilot/watchlist, not proof or leader.

profiles.name: JLL Spark
profiles.why: Illustrates strategic capital plus customer/distribution access and why built-environment startups need venture clients.
profiles.boundary: A portfolio membership or investment number is not product adoption, customer ROI or a recommendation to invest.

profiles.name: 31VENTURES
profiles.why: Strong developer-led venture-client/CVC comparator, particularly relevant to JCX’s Japanese collaboration narrative.
profiles.boundary: Activity counts are company-reported and not financial returns; keep program record separate from portfolio companies.

profiles.name: Saudi-PropTech-Hub-REGA
profiles.why: Adds public-sector/regulatory innovation context and a possible sandbox analogue for built-environment technology.
profiles.boundary: It is a program, not a vendor or startup outcome; government/program evidence does not prove cohort traction.

profiles.name: MetaProp portfolio
profiles.why: Broad investor/ecosystem discovery lens for market signals, data/trust and startup sourcing.
profiles.boundary: Portfolio count/capital figures are investor-reported; no company-level product or deployment conclusions should be made from membership.

profiles.name: Katerra
profiles.why: Essential cautionary case on factories, capex, working capital, vertical integration and construction-scale economics.
profiles.boundary: Include as a historical lesson, not an active competitor, product recommendation or blanket judgment that its technology had no value.

profiles.name: Sidewalk Labs / Quayside
profiles.why: Makes legitimacy, data governance, public purpose, scope and phasing part of the technology narrative.
profiles.boundary: Do not reduce termination to a single “technology failed” explanation; preserve documented cause, context and interpretation separately.

profiles.name: WeWork
profiles.why: Demonstrates that digital experience cannot repair fixed leases, utilization and capital-structure exposure.
profiles.boundary: Include as restructuring/business-model history, not as a PropTech product quality score or current operating benchmark.

profiles.name: PlanGrid
profiles.why: Shows acquired-product continuity and why acquired brands/products need lineage instead of being erased or counted as active standalone competitors.
profiles.boundary: Keep pre-acquisition identity and successor relationship explicit; do not conflate historical product status with current Autodesk product claims.

profiles.name: KE Holdings / Beike
profiles.why: Closes the mainland-China gap with an integrated online/offline housing transaction, brokerage, renovation and services comparator.
profiles.boundary: Filing-scale revenue and platform metrics are company-reported; keep KE Holdings, Beike and Lianjia brand/legal scopes distinct and do not infer technology-caused performance.

profiles.name: ALICE Technologies
profiles.why: Adds construction simulation and optioneering across schedules, resources, BIM and scenario choices—different from retrospective field capture.
profiles.boundary: Optimization benefits depend on schedule/WBS/BIM quality; customer stories and product claims are not universal realized outcomes.

profiles.name: SmartPM Technologies
profiles.why: Makes continuous schedule quality, delay, compression and portfolio-level project controls explicit.
profiles.boundary: Customer quotations and avoided-delay/dispute benefits are vendor-hosted; require consistent CPM data and a JCX baseline.

profiles.name: Togal.AI
profiles.why: Closes the automated takeoff/estimating gap and separates plan analysis from generic document chat.
profiles.boundary: Accuracy and speed claims are vendor-reported and vary by trade, drawing quality and review workflow.

profiles.name: Building Transparency
profiles.why: Introduces EC3 as open embodied-carbon/EPD infrastructure connecting design, procurement, policy and software integrations.
profiles.boundary: EC3 outcomes depend on EPD availability, boundaries, baselines and procurement practice; nonprofit/partner results remain attributed.

profiles.name: Sublime Systems
profiles.why: Represents a fully electrified electrochemical cement pathway and the pilot-to-commercial manufacturing challenge.
profiles.boundary: Planned commercial capacity, mature-scale cost and performance claims remain forward-looking or company-reported until scope-specific review.

profiles.name: Biomason
profiles.why: Adds biology-derived cement, producer partnership and qualified-factory commercialization as a distinct materials pathway.
profiles.boundary: Company statements on carbon, performance and manufacturing require standards, capacity, feedstock and economic diligence.

profiles.name: Brick & Bolt
profiles.why: Highly relevant South Asian model for productizing fragmented design-to-build work through managed contractors, milestone payments, quality checks and digital tracking.
profiles.boundary: Company scale and quality claims are not independent proof; city economics, complaints, contractor controls and service intensity matter.
